research_method.claude: Mixed methods: survey (multiple-choice, Likert, open-text; ~7 min; 3,500 invited, 530 responses, 15%) plus qualitative insights from interviews (10 developers, 20 engineering leads, a handful of Microsoft engineers) and observation of 23 Java developers using GitHub Copilot; focus groups mentioned in the methodology
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: survey (530 of 3,500), qualitative interviews (10 developers, 20 engineering leads), focus groups, observational study of 23 Java developers; cross-sectional; also lists a controlled study with 8 developers
research_method.value: Mixed-methods study: cross-sectional online survey structured by the SPACE dimensions (multiple-choice, Likert-scale and open-text items; 3,500 invited, 530 responses, 15% response rate), plus interviews with 10 professional developers and 20 engineering leads, observation of 23 experienced Java developers on accelerator and exploratory tasks with GitHub Copilot, and interviews with a handful of Microsoft engineers; focus groups mentioned in the methodology
research_method.note: NotebookLM counts the controlled study of 8 developers in the sample; Claude notes it is research by Sara Chizari at Microsoft, cited and not the authors' data, so it is omitted. Analysis is descriptive (percentages, mean agreement).

context.claude: Industry; Microsoft sample from a randomized pool of U.S. individual contributors plus an external sample from 15+ companies; 530 survey responses (>80% Microsoft)
context.nlm: 'Mixed' (>80% Microsoft developers; external participants from 15+ companies, e.g. Airbnb, Atlassian, DoorDash, Meta, Netflix, Reddit, Yelp); internal sample restricted to the U.S.
context.value: industry; Microsoft (>80% of survey participants, randomized pool of U.S. individual contributors) plus developers from at least 15 other companies (e.g., Airbnb, Atlassian, Charles Schwab, DoorDash, JetBrains, Meta, Netflix, Reddit, Yelp); 530 survey respondents, 10 developers and 20 engineering leads interviewed, 23 Java developers observed
context.note: NotebookLM's 'Mixed' label refers to Microsoft plus external companies; all participants are from industry.

cat_productivity.note: Borderline: both list SPACE Performance/Activity/Efficiency and 'more productive' items, but all are Likert self-reports, i.e. perceived productivity (counted under survey); coding-speed results are cited from other studies.

cat_collaboration.note: Survey item on ability to collaborate with teammates (48% agree) plus interview findings on fewer interruptions and higher-value team conversations.

cat_satisfaction.note: SPACE Satisfaction item (62% say AI enhances job satisfaction).

cat_activity.note: Both tag the SPACE Activity item (perceived task throughput) and self-reported AI-use frequency as Activity; neither is repository activity.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM tags perceived customer value (SPACE Performance) 'Delivery / Performance'; it is a Likert item, not a delivery metric.

cat_devex.note: DevEx framework not used; NotebookLM's 'DevEx' tags are generic.

evidence.quote: we conducted a mixed-methods research study combining survey data with qualitative insights derived from interviews and focus groups.

The survey consisted of a mix of multiple-choice questions, Likert-scale ratings, and open-text prompts. The core questions aimed to assess how AI tools impact developers’ experiences across the SPACE dimensions.
The survey was distributed to 3,500 individuals; 530 responses were received, yielding a response rate of 15 percent
we interviewed 10 professional developers and 20 engineering leads about the impact LLMs were having on their software development teams and observed 23 experienced Java developers
evidence.loc: PDF p. 3 (Customer Interviews and Observational Studies)

evidence.quote: More than 80 percent of the study participants were from Microsoft, but developers from at least 15 other companies were represented
The Microsoft sample was drawn from a randomized pool of developers within Microsoft, filtered to include individual contributors in the U.S., excluding those in finance, legal, or HR.

This article presents findings from a mixed-methods study examining how developers perceive AI’s influence across the dimensions of the SPACE framework: Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Collaboration, and Efficiency.
The survey was conducted in August 2024, using Microsoft Forms.
fewer than half of AI adopters (48 percent) agreed that AI has improved their ability to collaborate with teammates.
71 percent of AI adopters believe these tools help them deliver customer value, and 62 percent say AI enhances their job satisfaction.
